references.text: One of the brothers discovers his money in his sack when they stop for the night. This is the direct consequence of Joseph's command in 42:25 to put the money back into their sacks.
When the brothers empty their sacks at home, everyone finds their money there – the result of Joseph's order in 42:25.

Jacob instructs his sons to take back the money they found in their sacks, along with double the amount, to buy more grain. This directly follows the action in 42:25 where Joseph ordered that the money be returned.
Joseph orders his servant to put the money back into the brothers' sacks again, together with the silver cup. This reflects his earlier action in 42:25 when he also returned their money.
Joseph gives the brothers provisions for the journey (צידה לדרך), the same expression as in 42:25, when he reveals his identity and sends them home to bring Jacob.
The source verse summarizes the execution of the order given in detail in this verse; both show Joseph's secret action to test the brothers.
This verse expands on the same order as in the source verse by introducing the cup, which forms the basis for the theological climax of the story.
This verse provides the overarching theological context (God's providence through Joseph) of which the specific action in the source verse is a part.
